adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Turkey - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's Turkey country overview states the national framework every visitor to Adana Province stands under: same-sex sexual activity has been legal since 1858 (Ottoman penal code) and transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988, when gender reassignment surgery became legal; Turkey has no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity, and LGBTQ people are barred from serving openly in the military; same-sex relationships receive no legal recognition - marriage, civil unions and domestic partnerships are unavailable - and same-sex couples cannot adopt jointly or as individuals. The page carries no Adana-specific content, so it supplies only the countrywide baseline against which the record's 'no province-specific regime' assessment sits.
